name: Blueprint Custom Apparel
old_description: Exceptional printing quality with personalized service from real experts. Bulk orders for trade shows, businesses, and events.
about:
Blueprint Custom Apparel was established in 2019 in Derry, New Hampshire. The company operates from its New England base, providing custom-branded apparel and promotional products to a range of organizational clients.

The shop specializes in screen printing and embroidery, producing custom sweatshirts, jackets, hats, T-shirts, and a variety of branded accessories such as outerwear, workwear, and safety gear. Its services cover the full decoration process, from artwork preparation to final stitching or ink application, serving both small-run and bulk orders.

Blueprint works with small businesses, schools, U.S. government agencies, universities, enterprises, and startups, supplying apparel for trade shows, corporate events, and everyday uniform programs. The customer list reflects a focus on institutional and commercial buyers seeking consistent branding across multiple garment types.

The company emphasizes a direct, account-based approach: each client is assigned a dedicated sales representative to manage orders from quote through delivery. Blueprint also highlights its commitment to materials, craftsmanship, and repeatable quality, positioning its New England production as a mark of local excellence.

about:
Mahogany House Woodworks, operating as Boise Custom Furniture, is based in Boise, Idaho, and was founded in 2001 by James Barrett. Barrett came from a construction and high-end home building background before turning his lifelong passion for woodworking into a full-time shop. The business began with a focus on custom furniture built to last, using responsibly sourced materials and clean building methods.

The company designs and builds a range of custom wood products including dining tables, coffee tables, beds, headboards, bookshelves, floating shelves, adjustable desks, workstations, and commercial furniture for restaurants. They also produce custom wood countertops, butcher blocks, and cutting boards, and offer furniture engraving. All pieces are handcrafted in their Idaho shop, with an emphasis on practical design and durable joinery.

Mahogany House serves residential clients throughout Idaho and surrounding areas, as well as commercial customers such as restaurants and offices. Past projects include large bookcases for homes, bar tops for commercial spaces, and custom cutting boards for gifts. The shop works with domestic hardwoods, notably maple and walnut, to create pieces intended as heirlooms.

Barrett positions the shop as an alternative to mass-produced furniture, emphasizing handcrafted construction, responsible material use, and a collaborative design process that provides clients with updates and photos during fabrication. The company offers free quotes and aims to deliver furniture that fits the client's budget and space.

name: Bond's Brewing Company-Buffalo
old_description: At Bond’s Brewing Company, our standard beers offer a little something for everyone, ensuring that every guest finds a brew they love. Crafted with high-quality ingredients, each beer highlights our dedication to excellence and balance. We strive to keep these favorites on tap year-round, providing a consistent selection of well-crafted brews that you can count on for any occasion.
about:
Founded in 2019 in Laramie, Wyoming, Bond's Brewing Company began as a passion project to craft unique, high-quality beer and foster a welcoming community space. The founders are not publicly named, and ownership structure has not been disclosed. From the start, the brewery focused on developing its own distinct recipes, aiming to reflect a dedication to craftsmanship and flavor in every pint.

The company produces a lineup of standard beers available year-round across its two Wyoming taprooms in Laramie and Buffalo, along with seasonal offerings. Its portfolio includes styles such as a red ale, fruited wheat ale, kolsch, Scottish ale, and hop-forward pale ale, all brewed with ingredients like specialty malts, Yakima Valley hops, and fresh fruit. In 2023, the Buffalo location expanded the concept by adding a craft cocktail program made with high-quality ingredients, including house-made mixes such as a clam-juice Michelada and a pickle-juice variant. The brewery operates as both a production facility and a hospitality venue, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

Bond's Brewing serves locals and visitors seeking a community-oriented craft beverage experience. Its beers and cocktails are sold directly through its taprooms, and the company collaborates with other small businesses for events and partnerships. The brand positions itself within Wyoming's growing craft beverage scene, targeting craft beer enthusiasts, tourists, and residents looking for a gathering place.

The company states that community is at the core of its mission, viewing beer as an experience that brings people together. It emphasizes innovation, quality, and a commitment to contributing to the vibrant culture of Wyoming. The addition of cocktails in Buffalo reflects a desire to offer guests more options while maintaining the same creative standards applied to its beer.

name: BorgWarner Inc.
old_description: Industrial applications are evolving - and so are we. BorgWarner applies deep engineering expertise and advanced manufacturing capabilities to deliver solutions tailored to today’s industrial performance requirements.
about:
BorgWarner Inc. is headquartered in Hanover Park, Illinois. The company designs and manufactures systems for industrial and automotive applications, applying deep engineering expertise and advanced manufacturing capabilities to deliver solutions tailored to evolving industrial performance requirements.

Its product portfolio centers on battery energy storage systems (BESS), including generator battery systems, uninterruptible power supply units, and turbine generator systems. The company operates a production and service footprint across North America and Europe, with over 5 GWh of production capacity supported by a global supply base for cells and components. Core processes encompass full mechanical, electrical, testing, and validation capabilities, engineering services, and remanufacturing to extend product life. A removable electronics unit (RCB) enables easy service and repair.

BorgWarner serves industrial energy storage markets, providing stationary energy storage based on high-energy NMC battery technology for grid interaction and energy optimization. Customers deploy modular platforms ranging from rack-level backup to multi-megawatt-hour installations, addressing needs from seconds to hours of discharge duration.

The company differentiates itself through a cell-agnostic hardware and software architecture, automotive-grade battery management with redundant safety architecture, and a common hardware foundation that enables rapid deployment across power and energy scales.

name: Boston Electronics
old_description: SiC photodiode UV sensors and probes meet the demanding needs for lamp monitoring and control in water, air, sun, surface, curing and instrument applications.
about:
Boston Electronics operates from Brookline, Massachusetts. For forty years it has served as a distributor of electro-optical solutions, though a specific founding year is not disclosed.

The firm distributes advanced electro-optical components and specialized systems for microscopy, offering a broad portfolio that includes UV sensors and probes (SiC photodiodes), UV LEDs (255–405 nm), infrared detectors and imaging arrays (InGaAs PIN/APD, InAsSb, T2SLS), terahertz sources and imagers (QCL-based), photon-counting modules (TCSPC/FLIM), quantum cascade lasers, and laboratory instrumentation such as blackbody sources and laser power meters. It provides knowledgeable application support to help customers select and integrate these technologies.

Customers span environmental monitoring, process control, scientific instrumentation, life sciences and biomedical technologies, building and home automation, security and surveillance, and microscopy. The company works with researchers and manufacturers developing products for water and air purification, curing, lidar, thermal imaging, and spectroscopy.

Boston Electronics positions itself as a specialist in photo-detection and photon generation, representing manufacturers worldwide—including Hamamatsu, Becker & Hickl, Alpes Lasers, and Gentec-EO—to bring advantaged, unique-performance solutions to a broad market. Its stated differentiator is close collaboration with customers to address sensor requirements across diverse applications.

name: Boulder Furniture Arts
old_description: HEY, WE'RE BFA — CHAMPIONS OF SIMPLICITY, BASED IN BOULDER SINCE 1985. OUR FURNITURE IS BUILT FROM UNMATCHED AMERICAN HARDWOOD AND DESIGNED FOR LIFELONG JOY.
about:
Boulder Furniture Arts, a fine furniture design and build studio, has operated from Boulder, Colorado since its founding in 1985. The company remains independently owned, though no specific ownership structure such as family or veteran ownership is publicly disclosed. It began as a workshop dedicated to time-honored craftsmanship and has maintained a continuous presence in the same city for nearly four decades.

The firm produces two distinct lines: BFA Classic, a collection of largely unchanged designs dating back to 1985, and BFA Create, a custom arm that develops one-of-a-kind pieces including live-edge tables, built-in cabinetry, and mixed-material installations such as walnut-and-steel podiums or resin river tables. Production follows a 1-person-1-piece fabrication model supported by a 10-year apprenticeship program, with finishing limited to hand-rubbed oils and custom-matched commercial options. The shop also handles delivery, full-service installation, shipping, and a lifetime care program covering repair, refinishing, disassembly, and relocation.

Clients range from architects and interior designers who require precise collaboration to residents and families seeking heirloom-quality furnishings. The company also serves institutional leaders, artists, and environmentally conscious buyers who value carbon-storing materials. Projects have included custom DJ podiums, expandable pedestal tables, and conference-room installations, though specific brand names are not disclosed.

Boulder Furniture Arts distinguishes itself by sourcing all hardwoods within a two-day drive of its shop, guaranteeing every piece for life, and rejecting surplus inventory. The founders frame the business as an “old-school working art house run by people who give a damn,” emphasizing analog modern aesthetics, playful restraint, and a direct maker-to-client relationship.

name: Boxcar Woody (Reclaimed Lumber)
old_description: During those pioneering years, one car stood out among the rest, almost as important as the locomotive engine itself: the boxcar. Not just because of the versatility for the freight it could carry, but because of the connection with humanity it offered. The typical boxcar doubled as a passenger car for the ticketless. It was even sometimes left behind in those newly founded towns as a shelter or, for others, a home. It provided an escape for those wanting to run from his or her current predicament or a ride to a better life. Often, the boxcar’s walls were a sounding board for a newly penned song or where a life drew its very first and, sometimes, sadly, last breath. The American Boxcar was all of this and more to both early Americans and Immigrants alike.
about:
Boxcar Woody operates from Stockyards City in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The business traces its roots to 2015, when the founders of Boxcar Revival embarked on a road trip to salvage materials from retired American boxcars. That experience inspired the creation of Boxcar Woody, a venture dedicated to reclaiming authentic freight lumber and giving it new life in homes and businesses nationwide.

The company selects, mills, and finishes reclaimed boxcar and cargo wood, as well as whiskey barrel staves, in its Oklahoma workshop. From these materials it produces raw lumber, countertops, mantels, and a range of finished goods including dining tables, chairs, barstools, lighting, barn doors, and accessories. Each piece is handcrafted and can be made to order in custom sizes, with no two items exactly alike.

Boxcar Woody serves residential and commercial customers, including homeowners, designers, and contractors. Its reclaimed wood has been used for kitchen countertops, island tops, bathroom vanities, sliding barn doors, bar tops with waterfall edges, and exterior tables. The company also offers a line of whiskey barrel products such as chairs, barrels, and serving trays.

The founders started Boxcar Woody to preserve the legacy of the American railroads by turning historic materials into functional, lasting pieces. They emphasize quality craftsmanship and the unique character that comes from decades of service on the rails, positioning the reclaimed lumber as a connection to the nation’s transportation history.

old_description: Boyko Inc. was formed in August of 1987 as a USDA food manufacturing plant. The company was founded by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko. This family owned and operated corporation manufactured bakery and meat products. Within a short period of time, Boyko Inc. started developing and manufacturing additional food products. Boyko Inc. has worked with numerous clients in developing and manufacturing products that are well suited for their individual needs. about:
Boyko Inc. was founded in August 1987 in Stanton, North Dakota, by brothers Ron and Tom Boyko as a USDA‑inspected food manufacturing plant. The family‑owned corporation initially produced bakery and meat products before expanding into additional food items.

After two decades of manufacturing, the company sold its production operations in 2006 to focus on the used equipment market. Since 1996 Boyko has bought and sold used food‑processing machinery, and by 2002 it was doing so full‑time, sourcing equipment at auctions nationwide and partnering with auction firm Schneider Industries. Today the firm operates as a distributor and service provider, offering equipment listings, consignment sales, liquidations, asset‑management programs, technical support, and process‑plant consulting for food‑processing facilities.

The company serves food‑manufacturing customers across the processing industry, helping them acquire or dispose of equipment such as mixers, ovens, conveyors, packaging lines, and freezing systems. Its client base includes plants seeking individual machines or complete production lines, though no specific customers are named in public materials.

Boyko emphasizes its manufacturing heritage as a differentiator, stating that its background gives the team a diverse understanding of the requirements, challenges, and goals of food‑processing companies. The family‑owned business cites a mission to provide efficient, reliable service with the utmost integrity.
